answer: A graph trust protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by routing reputation across an agent endorsement trellis. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of obtaining scarce trust edges from established peers, throttling influence during an automated registration tide. Score attenuation across a bounded topological horizon prevents isolated clusters from fabricating credibility. However, this design imposes severe cold-start penalties on honest newcomers and structurally favors incumbent cartels.
